'''Tràkata''' was a style of [[Lightsaber combat/Legends|lightsaber combat]] developed for taking advantage of a lightsaber's ability to be turned on and off, a unique quality in a [[Melee weapon/Legends|melee weapon]]. Created by a [[Jedi Consular]] in the days of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Old Republic]] to compensate for weaknesses with using a [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]], it was based on quickly shutting off then re-igniting the blade, thus creating the possibility to confuse one's opponents, allowing for diversionary feints in combat. Mixed with [[Jar'Kai/Legends|Jar'Kai]], Tràkata was extremely effective even against multiple opponents.

==Known moves and maneuvers==
===Pass the Blade===
The duelist deactivated their blade as they attack, bypassing the opponent's block before igniting it into the helpless foe.<ref name="JATM">''[[Jedi Academy Training Manual]]''</ref>

===Unbalancing Block===
The duelist caught the opponent's blade with their own before momentarily deactivating it, causing the opponent to stumble and leave themselves open.<ref name="JATM" />

==Applications==
Unspecified examples:
#[[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi]] [[Jedi Master/Legends|Master]] [[Kao Cen Darach]] employed this or a similar technique to great effect during his fight with the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] [[Sith Lord/Legends|Lord]] [[Darth Vindican|Vindican]] and his apprentice, [[Darth Malgus|Malgus]], wherein he lost his life.<ref name="Return trailer">{{TORweb|url=info/media/trailers/return|text="Return"|int=Return (cinematic trailer)}}</ref>
#Members of the [[New Jedi Order]] known to employ this technique such as Jedi Master [[Mara Jade Skywalker]].<ref name="NJO Sourcebook">''[[The New Jedi Order Sourcebook]]''</ref>

Specified examples:
#Though not a Jedi, during [[Prince/Legends|Prince]] [[Xizor/Legends|Xizor's]] duel with the [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Jax Pavan]], in which Xizor had taken Pavan's [[Jax Pavan's lightsaber|lightsaber]] and Pavan was using a [[Jax Pavan's lightwhip|lightwhip]], Xizor performed a somersault over Jax. The Jedi wrapped the [[Lightwhip/Legends|lightwhip]] around his lightsaber but before he could pull it from Xizor's hands, Xizor disengaged the lightsaber causing the whip's cord to fall and forcing Jax to move out of the way as to not get hit. Once Xizor landed he powered the blade again and continued his duel with Pavan.<ref name="CNI:JT">''[[Coruscant Nights I: Jedi Twilight]]''</ref>
#Jedi Master [[Corran Horn/Legends|Corran Horn]] used a variant of this technique during the [[Yuuzhan Vong]] [[Yuuzhan Vong War|War]]; one notable occurrence being while he was [[Battle of Ithor|battling]] [[Shedao Shai]] on [[Ithor/Legends|Ithor]]. During the battle, Horn and Shai were locked in combat, and Horn deactivated his lightsaber then reignited it into Shedao Shai, killing the temporary [[Supreme Commander (Yuuzhan Vong rank)|Supreme Commander]].<ref name="DarkTideI">''[[The New Jedi Order: Dark Tide I: Onslaught]]''</ref>
#During her duel with [[Ben Skywalker]], [[Sith apprentice/Legends|Sith apprentice]] [[Tahiri Veila]] used this technique to great effect. Skywalker forced her lightsaber aside, so Tahiri switched her lightsaber off and on so fast Skywalker barely had time to react, allowing her to extend the blade to where his throat had been just moments before.<ref name="Invincible">''[[Legacy of the Force: Invincible]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
Tràkata was a [[fanon]] creation that was brought into continuity by the ''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game Saga Edition Core Rulebook]]''.

Although not an official form in [[Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Jedi Academy|''Jedi Knight: Jedi Academy'']], turning off [[Jaden Korr]]'s lightsaber increased the potency of [[Force lightning/Legends|Force lightning]], [[Telekinesis/Legends#Force Grip|Force Grip]], and [[Telekinesis/Legends#Force Push|Force Push]], which can be seen as use of Tràkata. Additionally, in ''[[Star Wars: Battlefront II]]'', [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]] turns off his blade to free his hand when using Force lightning.
